changes: Map SVG transform cache: country geometry drawn once at the reference camera, per-frame affine transform on one <g> (src/map/project.mjs cameraMatrix, src/map/runtime.mjs, src/renderer/compile.mjs).
Frame dedup: Node-side visual key per frame (src/renderer/framekey.mjs); identical frames reuse one PNG (HME_DEDUP=0 disables).
Real-time preview: --profile preview-rt / --realtime, CDP screencast + MediaRecorder-free JPEG sampling, output preview-rt.mp4, labelled non-deterministic (src/renderer/render.mjs renderRealtime).
Profiles: final is now supersample 1.5, preset medium, CRF 14; final-max keeps the old ceiling (supersample 2, preset slow, CRF 14). ffmpeg threads unpinned, 2 capture workers.
machine: Linux VM, 7.7 GB RAM, 4 cores, shared load (other agents running). Times are wall seconds on this machine, not a clean bench. Load average at each render start is recorded per row.

determinism.map_sample_final_run_a_vs_run_b: Byte-identical video sha256 58b4d35b126b899a (run-a under load 17, run-b on the quiet machine, 65.2s) and all 240 frame hashes identical. New path with map cache + dedup.
determinism.unit_test: Renderer tests: determinism on previs, 12 frames, two runs match (in the 23-test renderer suite, all pass).
determinism.v3_vs_v3q_all_9: All 9 scene/profile videos are byte-identical between the loaded v3 runs (load 13-21) and the quiet v3q runs (load 2-9): same sha256 for every pair. Output does not depend on machine load.

preview_rt.note: Real-time preview works end to end (valid 240-frame 1920x1080 h264, all seeks reached, labelled non-deterministic) but does NOT hit the under-20s target on the loaded VM: 228.3s (v1 sampling) and 185.5s (v2 per-seek sampling) for a 10s scene-min clip. Cause: each seek waits on 2 rAF ticks and the compositor runs at ~1fps under load, so a seek takes ~0.9s vs the 41.7ms frame interval. Two preview runs give different video shas (c5404e2a vs c8296f73), as expected for a non-deterministic mode. Sampling bug found and fixed: v1 sampled the first 10s of screencast time, so the video was nearly static (inter-frame SSIM 0.9966-0.9992); v2 samples per seek, so the video shows the whole scene (inter-frame SSIM 0.9535).

quality_old_vs_new_map_sample.draft_same_profile: Old draft (sha 4ec4448e) vs new draft (sha 46c44950): 240 frames, SSIM mean 0.99997, min 0.99989, 0 frames below 0.99, PSNR mean 68.61 dB, min 52.07 dB. Profile unchanged, so this isolates the cache + dedup effect.
quality_old_vs_new_map_sample.final_profile_changed: Old final (sha 4db79517, supersample 2, preset slow) vs new final (sha 58b4d35b, supersample 1.5, preset medium): 240 frames, SSIM mean 0.99999, min 0.99996, 0 frames below 0.99, PSNR mean 72.2 dB, min 56.84 dB. Confounded by the profile change, but the pixels are still essentially identical.
quality_old_vs_new_map_sample.map_cache_12f_smoke: Cache on vs off, frames 100-112 (camera move): mean SSIM 0.99819, min 0.99771, PSNR mean 44.55 dB. PNG hashes differ (sub-pixel rounding), so the map-cache video sha differs from the legacy path even though the picture is the same to the eye.

tradeoffs: Preview-rt misses the under-20s target on the loaded VM (185-228s for a 10s clip). The seek/compositor rate under load is the bottleneck, not the preview design. On a quiet machine it would be faster, but that was not measured here.

Map cache is not byte-identical to the legacy path. The picture matches (SSIM 0.998-0.99999, PSNR 44-72 dB) but the video sha differs, because path coordinates are rounded at the reference camera and then transformed instead of being rounded at the frame camera. Two runs of the same (new) path are byte-identical; only old-vs-new differs.
Wall time is dominated by machine load, not the engine: map-sample final took 603.8s at load 17 and 65.2s at load ~2, same bytes out. Every wall number here must be read with its load_avg_1m.

Final is still over the 40s draft-predicate target for map (57.0s) and scene-min (51.1s) on the quiet machine; only text-sample final (37.5s) is under 40s. Final is 1.65x draft for map and 1.79x for scene-min (target 1.5x); text is 1.49x.
First-frame cost: the map cache adds ~0.5s at compile time (map-sample compile 0.61-0.63s steady vs 0.10-0.12s for scene-min with no map). Small against a 35-600s render.

Memory: peak process-tree RSS for a 12-frame map-sample draft render was 847 MB (new path) vs 1556 MB (old path) in single samples, but that gap is mostly Chromium allocator noise, not the cache: the PNG buffers for 12 frames are only ~20 MB. The real saving is at 240 frames, where dedup holds 149 unique PNGs instead of 240 (~135 MB fewer buffers for map-sample).

The SVG transform cache alone does not speed up capture: a 12-frame moving-camera smoke test was 170s (cache on) vs 139s (cache off), inside load noise. The rasterizer still re-rasterizes the transformed group each screenshot; the cache only saves the JS re-projection. The measured speedup comes from frame dedup plus the profile change, not from the SVG transform alone. A bitmap layer cache (rasterize once, drawImage per frame) is the next step if more speed is needed.

Code added: ~500 lines across src/renderer/framekey.mjs, src/renderer/render.mjs (dedup + preview), src/renderer/cli.mjs, src/renderer/report.mjs, src/map/project.mjs (cameraMatrix), src/map/runtime.mjs (base group), src/renderer/compile.mjs (refCam). Two new tests (framekey, camera-matrix) pass; 98 Node tests pass. The Python checker suite (13 tests) did not finish under load in this session (killed after 35+ min); the 11 layout tests passed in the earlier layout build.
verdict: FASTER with a named tradeoff. Quiet-machine renders are 2.5-4.8x faster than v1 (draft profiles, unchanged, are 2.5-3.1x faster from cache + dedup alone), determinism is proven byte-identical, and old-vs-new pixels match at SSIM 0.99997-0.99999. Tradeoffs: the real-time preview does not hit under-20s on the loaded VM (185-228s), and the map cache is not byte-identical to the legacy path (SSIM 0.998+, but a different video sha).
tool: headless-motion-engine (HyperFrames 0.9.20, GSAP 3.15.0, Node >= 20) with layer cache (map SVG transform cache + frame dedup) and real-time preview
